monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a heavy fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I press down on The Soft Edge, trying to convince the wide thing that it can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp point to bite. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did the slip slide beneath the soft memory while I was busy touching the pine tree? I set down a stone beside it, anchoring the slip to a memory of grit. Now the place feels crowded again, a drawing of stone pretending to be solid. I will lean harder on the flat line anyway, hoping the slip stays put while the card vibrates beneath my tired corner.

action.why: The slip feels like it's sliding beneath the soft memory while I was busy touching the pine tree, and the card hums too warm for a stable press.
